text.title: Design Docs Patterns Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end worked example for Design Docs Patterns: trigger fires, inputs gathered, artefact produced and validated against output contract. Followed by section-level examples of non-goals, alternatives and ADR extraction.

example.title: Happy-path application
example.trigger: Operator opens calendar slot named in Applies If; preconditions are met.
example.validation: Run scripts/validate-design-docs-patterns.py against the produced artefact. Expected exit 0 (ok).
example.downstream: Artefact handed off to the consumers named in Related; outcome reviewed at next iteration.

example.title: Un-anchored application
example.trigger: Operator skipped Applies If gate; preconditions not verified.
example.inputs: Free-text prose substitutes; no cited evidence.
example.validation: Validator returns non-zero with violation list per forbidden patterns in content/02-output-contract.xml.
example.downstream: Artefact rejected; consumers do not read; operator reruns with full preconditions.

example.title: Non-goals that are real scope boundaries
example.code:
## Non-Goals
- Real-time collaboration (multiple editors on the same doc simultaneously) — planned for v2 - Mobile-native UI — web-responsive layout is sufficient for initial release - Offline-first caching — requires service worker infrastructure not yet in place

example.title: Non-goals that state the obvious
example.code:
## Non-Goals
- We are not building the entire product at once - We will not rewrite everything in a new language
example.note: These are obvious and add no value. Non-goals must be specific scope boundaries that readers might actually assume are in scope.

example.title: Two genuine alternatives with why-not-chosen
example.code:
## Alternatives Considered
### Alternative 1: Event-driven with message queue
Use Kafka to decouple the write pipeline from downstream consumers.
- Pros: consumers can scale independently; producer is not blocked by slow consumers - Cons: adds operational complexity (Kafka cluster); introduces at-least-once delivery - Why not chosen: our current scale (100 RPS) does not justify the Kafka overhead; revisit if we exceed 10k RPS
### Alternative 2: Synchronous polling by consumers
Consumers poll an API endpoint for new records every 30 seconds.
- Pros: no new infrastructure; simple to implement and debug - Cons: up to 30s latency; polling adds unnecessary load at low event rates - Why not chosen: 30s latency violates NFR-2 (sub-5s delivery requirement)
